fact: The UN Economic Commission for Africa, through its Data Governance in Africa initiative, supported the Republic of the Congo in developing its National Data Governance Strategy through consultations and stakeholder engagements held in Brazzaville from 2 to 9 June 2026.

The UN Economic Commission for Africa, with GIZ and EU support and the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy, announced engagements on 2-9 June 2026 (assessment and consultations, a stakeholder workshop on 8 June, capacity building on 9 June) to support development of a National Data Governance Strategy, after a self-assessment found the country had no integrated national data governance strategy.

The UN Economic Commission for Africa reported that a stakeholder workshop of 60 participants, held in Brazzaville on 8-9 June 2026 after an assessment mission consulting 21 institutions, supported the drafting of the Republic of the Congo's National Data Governance Strategy, and that the ministry's chief of staff reaffirmed the government's commitment to put such a strategy in place.
